solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Abusive harangue from girl at a race

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
a tribe is a race or people

explanation.surface: Someone at a race meeting gets an earful of abuse from a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, abusive verbal attack, a long harangue.

clue.text: Seabed could become lower

indicators.note: the letters of the clue word could become a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: The ocean floor might sink further.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower someone or something in esteem or quality is to degrade them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Take gold initially to the French then a goddess

indicators.note: says the French piece is placed at the very start, before the rest

parts.note: in French 'to the' is au (à + le)
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin 'take', on prescriptions
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry gold to France and then to a goddess, like an offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold' tempts you to AU, but AU here is French 'to the'; gold is the heraldic OR. 'initially' puts the French piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora was the Roman goddess of the dawn.

clue.text: Find in lariat another kind of rope? Yes and no

indicators.note: tells you to look for the answer inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a lariat contains a second type of rope, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is the setter's joke: a riata is just another name for a lariat, so it is and is not another kind of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a lasso or lariat rope, used in the American West.

clue.text: Crowd's rising about deprivation of source of neroli, for example

indicators.note: the reversed crowd goes about, around, the next piece
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd; the 's is read as 'is'
a loss is a deprivation

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers in protest over being deprived of a perfume ingredient's source.
explanation.walkthrough: Neroli is an essential oil distilled from orange blossom, so the blossom is an example of its source.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange flowers are where neroli oil comes from, so a flower is an example of such a source.

clue.text: Rascal's one fish

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal; the 's is read as 'is'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rascal is described as a single fish, a slippery character.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, sea creatures served as seafood, so loosely fish.

clue.text: See Labour — regularly — like this

parts.note: to clock is slang for to see or notice
work is labour

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch the Labour Party, which works steadily in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party but is plain toil; the definition means 'like clockwork', the idiom for regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done with mechanical regularity are said to run like clockwork, a common idiom.

clue.text: Language of senior official

definitions.meaning: the standard spoken form of Chinese
a high-ranking bureaucrat, originally in imperial China

explanation.surface: The speech used by a top civil servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the main Chinese tongue and a powerful bureaucrat in imperial China or Whitehall.

clue.text: Kill Ray for his sporting equipment?

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for to kill them
a skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish

explanation.surface: A murderer called Ray needs his gear for some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' reads as a man's name but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot with a blade, worn for gliding on a rink, is a piece of sporting kit.

clue.text: Composer has a test for pear

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: A composer takes some test to identify a pear variety.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety check.
explanation.definitionFit: A bergamot is a variety of fine pear, as well as a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Softly cat makes a swoop

parts.note: p is piano, softly, in music
an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat creeps quietly before diving onto its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spring or swoop onto prey is a noun for the same sudden attack.

clue.text: Tool of aged in Algeria? On the contrary

indicators.note: the clue says one abbreviation goes within the other
reverses the roles: the country goes inside the age abbreviation, not the other way round

parts.note: ae is the abbreviation for aetatis, 'aged', on inscriptions
DZ is the international vehicle code for Algeria

explanation.surface: A query whether an old man's implement comes from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Went beyond authorisation in certain department

indicators.note: the permit goes inside the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
a pass is a permit or authorisation

explanation.surface: Someone overstepped their permit within a particular office.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass something is to exceed or go past it, so past tense matches.

clue.text: Habit of king to have light meal with no end of fuss

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: says the named letter is dropped from the meal

parts.note: a snack is a light meal

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word fuss

explanation.surface: A monarch's habit of grabbing a quick bite without any fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A knack is a learned skill or trick, a sense close to habit or way of doing something.

clue.text: Half the alphabet is something very small

definitions.text: Half the alphabet is something very small

parts.words: Half the alphabet is something very small
parts.note: half the alphabet is described as a range, from its first letter up to its thirteenth, and that phrase run together names a tiny particle

explanation.surface: A claim that half of the alphabet is tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the classic emblem of minuteness, a tiny particle of matter.

clue.text: Moroccan dynasty with monarch in Spain

parts.note: the Tang was a Chinese imperial dynasty
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A North African royal line allied with a king living in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moroccan' suggests the dynasty is Moroccan, but it is Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine also means a native of Tangier, the Moroccan port, which gave the fruit its name.

clue.text: One over-concerned with himself got entered in wrong site

indicators.note: the second word goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of site are put wrong, rearranged, to give EIST

explanation.surface: Someone self-obsessed blundered into the wrong location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' and 'himself' make the surface sound like a person getting lost; the definition is the whole first phrase, a self-centred person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person preoccupied with self-importance is a classic self-centred individual.

clue.text: Corresponding in sound from donkey close to insect

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
on can mean near or close to, as in 'on the coast'
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A noise comes from a donkey standing next to a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonant describes words whose vowel sounds match, a rhyming-like resemblance.

clue.text: Fruit important artist sent to Germany and Spain

parts.note: big means important
ARA is an Associate of the Royal Academy, a painter
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A distinguished painter is dispatched to two European countries with some produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The bigarade is the bitter Seville orange, a citrus fruit used in marmalade.

clue.text: It's used for catching fish in bowler

definitions.meaning: a revolving lure on an angler's line
in cricket, a bowler who makes the ball turn

explanation.surface: Fishing tackle found in a bowler hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests the hat but is a cricket bowler who spins the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an angler's revolving lure and a cricketer who imparts turn on the ball.

clue.text: Feeling of euphoria when game's hot

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game; the 's gives S
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Elation when a match is heating up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a sudden surge of excitement or pleasure, a high.

clue.text: Benefit of drink

definitions.meaning: as in 'for the benefit of', for someone's good

explanation.surface: The good that comes from a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both behalf or benefit ('for his good') and Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: Spanish city finds wickedness in psalter regularly

indicators.note: the wickedness is put inside the regular letters
take every other letter of the word psalter, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: A city discovers sin in a book of psalms, found again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is the capital of Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Future partner requires money without warning essentially

indicators.note: says the next letter is removed from the money word

parts.note: finance is money or funds

indicators.note: takes the central letter, the essence, of the word warning

explanation.surface: A prospective spouse needs cash without any notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancé is the man someone is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Possibly haunts extremely French island

indicators.note: the letters of haunts could possibly form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A ghost may frequent a very French island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' belongs to the definition: Ushant (Ouessant) is the westernmost point of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushant is the island off Brittany marking France's far western tip.

clue.text: Old wise American

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: An elderly, wise person from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Excessive neckwear for such ages?

parts.note: an extravagant number of neckties, seven of them, read as a decade of life

explanation.surface: Wearing too many ties is a habit of a particular age.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SEVEN TIES, an excessive amount of neckwear; whole, it names the decade of ages from seventy to seventy-nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade of life from seventy to seventy-nine is the period these ages fall in.

clue.text: Main body left central point

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: The principal part of something has left its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly button is figuratively the centre or hub of anything, as in 'navel of the world'.

clue.text: Accountant spies tree

parts.note: ACA is an Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper notices a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spies' looks like a verb, seeing, but it is a noun for the agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of thorny trees and shrubs, including wattles.

clue.text: Strong attachment to the six counties in South American country

indicators.note: the attachment and the counties go within the South American abbreviation

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South America
love is a strong attachment
Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI, is made up of six counties

explanation.surface: Deep affection for Northern Ireland found in a South American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American country' is a false unit: the definition is just 'country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a Central European nation, once part of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: One could live in this empty township, we hear

indicators.note: the two letters are said aloud, giving the sound of the answer
an empty word keeps only its outer letters, its contents removed

explanation.surface: A deserted town's dwellings, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves T and P, the outside letters of 'township'; spoken, they give the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A teepee is a conical tent dwelling of Plains peoples, somewhere a person could live.

clue.text: Recklessly determined he will get 13

parts.note: 'll is the contracted form of will
the answer at 13 across means aptitude, and a bent is an aptitude

explanation.surface: A man is set to acquire a flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is KNACK, and a bent (a natural flair) is a knack.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means fiercely set on something regardless of consequences.
